'''Arena Hinekura Sherburd Williams'''<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Husband |first=Dale |date=5 September 2020 |title=Arena Williams: Making changes from the inside |url=https://e-tangata.co.nz/korero/arena-williams-making-changes-from-the-inside/ |access-date=18 October 2023 |website=E-Tangata |language=en-NZ}}</ref> (born 1990) is a New Zealand [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]] politician. She has been a [[Member of parliament|Member of Parliament]] in the [[New Zealand House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] for the [[Manurewa (New Zealand electorate)|Manurewa electorate]] since [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020]].<ref name="40 new MPs">{{Cite news |via=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |title=Election 2020: The 40 diverse new MPs entering Parliament |url= https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/news/vote-2020/election-2020-the-forty-newcomers-entering-parliament/ |date=18 October 2020 |access-date=16 November 2020 |work=[[Newstalk ZB]] |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201022040442/https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/news/vote-2020/election-2020-the-forty-newcomers-entering-parliament/ |archive-date=22 October 2020}}</ref>

==Early life, career and family==
Williams is affiliated with the [[Māori people|Māori]] [[iwi]] of [[Te Aitanga-a-Māhaki]], [[Ngāi Tūhoe]] and [[Ngāi Tahu]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12352951 |title=Election 2020: PM Jacinda Ardern launches campaign to keep Māori seats |work=NZ Herald |date=2 August 2020}}</ref> Her parents are doctor Jacqueline Allan (Ngāi Tahu) and educator, broadcaster, and former [[Papakura City|Papakura city]] councillor Sir [[Haare Williams]] (Ngāi Tūhoe and Te Aitanga-a-Māhaki).<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Husband |first=Dale |date=23 November 2019 |title=Haare Williams: A child of the community |url=https://e-tangata.co.nz/korero/haare-williams-a-child-of-the-community/ |access-date=18 October 2023 |website=E-Tangata}}</ref><ref name=Pellegrino_2023 /> She grew up in [[Papakura]] and spoke [[Māori language|Māori]] as a child.<ref name=":0" /> Williams attended [[Diocesan School for Girls, Auckland|Diocesan School for Girls]] in Auckland.<ref name=":0" />

Williams studied law and commerce at the [[University of Auckland]], and was active within the [[Princes Street Labour]]. In 2012 she was president of the [[Auckland University Students' Association]].<ref name="next wave">{{cite news |title=The next wave: Labour's Arena Williams |author=Hunt, Elle |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/the-wireless/371625/the-next-wave-labour-s-arena-williams |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=20 June 2014 |access-date=31 May 2020 }}</ref> In 2012 she and other university students staged a campus protest to highlight the issue of rising student debt. The under-dressed students begged people passing on the street for clothing, graphically depicting how students have to "borrow to live".<ref>{{cite news |title=Naked students protest debt |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/auckland/local-news/6513708/Naked-students-protest-debt |access-date=19 October 2020 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=3 March 2012 }}</ref><ref name="justice reform">{{cite news |last1=Keogh |first1=Brittany |title=Lawyer and new Labour MP for Manurewa Arena Williams to focus on justice reform |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/123068085/election-2020-lawyer-and-new-labour-mp-for-manurewa-arena-williams-to-focus-on-justice-reform |access-date=19 October 2020 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=18 October 2020}}</ref>

Williams began her career working as a [[Probation and parole officer|probation officer]] in [[Panmure, New Zealand|Panmure]], encountering many people in the court system for relatively minor offences, prompting her advocacy for justice reform.<ref name="justice reform" /> She also worked for law firm [[Chapman Tripp]].<ref name=":0" />

===Early political career===
Williams stood for the [[Hunua (New Zealand electorate)|Hunua]] electorate in the [[New Zealand House of Representatives]] in {{NZ election link|2014}} for the [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]] where she placed second, losing to [[Andrew Bayly]] by the large margin of 17,376 votes.<ref>{{cite web|author=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |url=http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2014/electorate-16.html |title=Official Count Results – Hunua |date=10 October 2014 |access-date=1 February 2016}}</ref> Aged 24 she was Labour's youngest candidate at that election.<ref name="next wave"/>

In November 2019 Williams was appointed as a member of the [[Waitematā District Health Board]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Board meeting |url=https://www.waitematadhb.govt.nz/assets/Documents/board/2019/WDHB-Open-Board-Meeting-Dec-2019.pdf |publisher=[[Waitematā District Health Board]] |access-date=19 October 2020 |page=28 |date=18 December 2019}}</ref>

Williams as well as Ian Dunwoodie both nominated to challenge [[Louisa Wall]] for the Labour Party selection for the seat of {{NZ electorate link|Manurewa}}, one of the safest [[New Zealand Labour Party#Voter base|red seats]] in the country.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newsroom.co.nz/2020/02/12/1028595/labours-louisa-wall-faces-challenge-for-manurewa-selection |title=Labour's Louisa Wall faces challenge for Manurewa selection |first=Dileepa |last=Fonseka |website=[[Newsroom (website)|Newsroom]] |date=12 February 2020 |access-date=29 May 2020}}</ref> The selection was scheduled to be held on 21 March 2020, but was delayed due to a complaint about whether some new party electorate branch members lived in Manurewa and were eligible to vote in the selection process.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12316599 |title=Labour delays Manurewa candidate selection to look at membership issues |first=Audrey |last=Young |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=13 March 2020 |access-date=29 May 2020}}</ref> In May, Wall's partner and lawyer Prue Kapua contacted the national party council, claiming that Williams's application was late, and warned that legal action would be taken if it was not rejected.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newsroom.co.nz/2020/05/11/1167589/legal-action-looms-over-labours-manurewa-selection |title=MP and Labour Party face court fight over Manurewa |first=Sam |last=Sachdeva |website=[[Newsroom (website)|Newsroom]] |date=11 May 2020 |access-date=29 May 2020}}</ref> The selection was rescheduled to 30 May, but Wall withdrew her application on 29 May, to instead run as a list-only candidate. Williams was selected as the Labour candidate.<ref name="pullsout">{{cite news |title=Labour's Louisa Wall pulls out of Manurewa selection |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=12335909 |access-date=29 May 2020 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]}}</ref>

===First term, 2020–2023===
During the [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020 general election]] held on 17 October, she beat National candidate Nuwi Samarakone by a margin of 17,179 votes.<ref name="40 new MPs" /><ref name="justice reform"/><ref>{{Cite web|date=6 November 2020|title=Manurewa - Official Result|url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-22.html|access-date=7 January 2021|publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}}</ref><ref><!-- this reference confirms that it's now 42 new members, giving Labour one new MP -->{{cite news |last1=Lynch |first1=Jenna |title=NZ Election 2020: Judith Collins will 'definitely not' stand down as leader despite National's crushing defeat |url= https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/11/nz-election-2020-judith-collins-will-definitely-not-stand-down-as-leader-despite-national-s-crushing-defeat.html |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201106055203/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/11/nz-election-2020-judith-collins-will-definitely-not-stand-down-as-leader-despite-national-s-crushing-defeat.html |url-status= dead |archive-date= 6 November 2020 |access-date=8 November 2020 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=6 November 2020}}</ref> In her first term, Williams served as a member of the justice committee, Māori affairs committee (including as deputy chairperson and chairperson) and the [[Pae Ora (Healthy Futures) Act 2022|Pae Ora legislation]] committee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Williams, Arena - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/members-of-parliament/williams-arena/ |access-date=18 October 2023 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref>

===Second term, 2023–present===
She was re-elected in Manurewa at the [[2023 New Zealand general election|2023 general election]], with a majority of 7,113 over National Party candidate Siva Kilari.<ref>{{cite web |title=Manurewa - Official Result |url= https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-22.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=11 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123104120/https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-22.html |archive-date=23 November 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> In late November 2023, Williams was appointed as Assistant Whip, and spokesperson for commerce and consumer affairs, building and construction, and state-owned enterprises in the [[Shadow Cabinet of Chris Hipkins]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Labour Party leader Chris Hipkins reveals new shadow Cabinet |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/503581/labour-party-leader-chris-hipkins-reveals-new-shadow-cabinet |access-date=11 December 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=30 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231204120147/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/503581/labour-party-leader-chris-hipkins-reveals-new-shadow-cabinet |archive-date=4 December 2023}}</ref> In a reshuffle in early March 2025, Williams gained the youth portfolio, retained the commerce and consumer affairs and building and construction portfolios, and lost the [[state-owned enterprise]]s portfolio.<ref>{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Russell |title=Chris Hipkins announces new Labour 'economic team', Tangi Utikere promoted |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/544048/chris-hipkins-announces-new-labour-economic-team-tangi-utikere-promoted |access-date=8 March 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=7 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250307011659/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/544048/chris-hipkins-announces-new-labour-economic-team-tangi-utikere-promoted |archive-date=7 March 2025}}</ref>

In late April 2026, Williams's private member's bill requiring banks and money transfer services to disclose international money transfer fees to customers passed its first reading with the support of all parties except the [[New Zealand National Party|National Party]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pullar-Strecker |first1=Tom |title=National the lone opponent to a bill supporters say could cut millions in bank fees |url=https://www.thepost.co.nz/business/360995036/national-may-be-lone-opponent-bill-designed-lower-foreign-exchange-fees |access-date=9 May 2026 |work=[[The Post (New Zealand newspaper)|The Post]] |date=29 April 2026|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Release: Labour Bill ending hidden transfer fees passes first reading |url=https://www.labour.org.nz/news/release-labour-bill-ending-hidden-transfer-fees-passes-first-reading/ |publisher=[[New Zealand Labour Party]] |access-date=9 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509013921/https://www.labour.org.nz/news/release-labour-bill-ending-hidden-transfer-fees-passes-first-reading/ |archive-date=9 May 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In September, during the [[2026 New Zealand general election|2026 election]] campaign, Williams announced Labour's plans for supermarket competition.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 September 2026 |title=Labour to split up supermarket wholesale and retail arms in first 100 days |url=https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/on-air/early-edition-with-ryan-bridge/audio/arena-williams-commerce-and-consumer-affairs-spokesperson-on-tackling-the-supermarket-duopoly/ |access-date=27 September 2026 |website=NewstalkZB }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=20 September 2026 |title=Nicola Willis v Arena Williams on the supermarket duopoly debate |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/nationals-nicola-willis-v-labours-arena-williams-on-the-supermarket-duopoly-debate/premium/E7MTLCO36ZAN5AX3GTIC3RXBTI/ |access-date=27 September 2026 |website=NZ Herald}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Williams is married to ex-lawyer Max Hardy.<ref name="justice reform" /> They have two children.<ref>{{Cite web |first1=Arena |last1= Williams |first2= Stuart |last2 =Smith |date=14 March 2025 |title=Arena Williams: A Prime Minister who sneers at struggling families has no idea what life is really like |url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/360614995/arena-williams-prime-minister-who-sneers-struggling-families-has-no-idea-what-life-really |access-date=27 September 2026 |website=Stuff}}</ref> She enjoys painting.<ref name=Pellegrino_2023>{{Cite web |last=Pellegrino |first=Nicky |date=27 May 2023 |title=MP & mum Arena Williams: it's a labour of love |website= [[The New Zealand Herald]] |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/lifestyle/mp-mum-arena-williams-its-a-labour-of-love/ZP4237URRRAR3O4DL7DGMEFNJU/ |access-date=27 September 2026}}</ref>

===Kāinga Ora advertisement===
In November 2021, the New Zealand social housing agency [[Kāinga Ora]] drew controversy after [[Newshub]] and [[Radio New Zealand]] reported that the agency had used Williams (a Labour Party candidate) in a taxpayer-funded advertisement in 2020, compromising its political neutrality. Kāinga Ora drew criticism from [[Minister of Housing (New Zealand)|Housing Minister]] [[Megan Woods]] and deputy Opposition Leader [[Nicola Willis]] on the grounds of professionalism and compromising its political neutrality.<ref>{{cite news |last1=O'Brien |first1=Tova |title=Kāinga Ora hid the fact it was using Labour candidate Arena Williams in taxpayer-funded advertising |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/11/kainga-ora-hid-the-fact-it-was-using-labour-candidate-arena-williams-in-taxpayer-funded-advertising.html |access-date=12 November 2021 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=10 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211111073617/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/11/kainga-ora-hid-the-fact-it-was-using-labour-candidate-arena-williams-in-taxpayer-funded-advertising.html |archive-date=11 November 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="RNZ 12 Nov 2021">{{cite news |title=National Party wants investigation into Kāinga Ora |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/455516/national-party-wants-investigation-into-kainga-ora |access-date=12 November 2021 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=11 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211111105746/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/455516/national-party-wants-investigation-into-kainga-ora |archive-date=11 November 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> Woods subsequently reported the agency to the [[Public Service Commission (New Zealand)|Public Service Commission]].<ref name="dobs in">{{cite news |last1=Lynch |first1=Jenna |title=Housing Minister Megan Woods dobs Kāinga Ora in to public service watchdog over cover-up |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/11/housing-minister-megan-woods-dobs-k-inga-ora-in-to-public-service-watchdog-over-cover-up.html |access-date=12 November 2021 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=11 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211111053229/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/11/housing-minister-megan-woods-dobs-k-inga-ora-in-to-public-service-watchdog-over-cover-up.html |archive-date=11 November 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref> The [[New Zealand National Party|National Party]] called for an investigation into Kāinga Ora, alleging a cover up and "culture of deceit."<ref name="RNZ 12 Nov 2021" /> Williams had informed Kāinga Ora of her political ambitions prior to the advertorial featuring her was paid for and published.<ref name="dobs in"/>
